clue.text: Chap set tree by meadow

indicators.note: by means next to, so the tree stands beside the meadow

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
a ley (or lea) is a poetic word for a meadow or pasture

explanation.surface: A man plants a tree beside a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashley is a man's first name, and a chap is any man, so the name is an example.

clue.text: Very excited; oxygen is found in abundance

parts.note: agog means eagerly excited
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An excited scientist notes that a gas is plentiful.
explanation.walkthrough: The semicolon hides the join: the first part plus the gas's symbol makes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A-go-go is an informal idiom meaning in great quantity, galore.

clue.text: White fish swallows wriggling eel

indicators.note: swallows means the fish takes the other letters into its middle

parts.note: huss is a name for dogfish sold for eating

indicators.note: wriggling describes the eel twisting about, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A white fish gulps down a squirming eel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White fish' looks like one phrase; 'White' is the definition and the fish is the huss. ELE (the eel mixed up) goes inside HUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without any colour can be called white, in the sense of colourless.

clue.text: Formation dance moves get homies jigging

indicators.note: jigging means bouncing about as in a jig, so these letters dance into a new order

explanation.surface: A group dance sees a bunch of friends bopping around.
explanation.walkthrough: An eightsome reel is a Scottish country dance for eight people in set formation.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome is a Scottish reel danced by eight people in a set pattern, so it is a formation dance.

clue.text: "Hell, Chomsky's turning round, Mr. President"

indicators.note: round means the turned name goes around the underworld
turning means the linguist's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Noam Chomsky is the American linguist
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and so hell

explanation.surface: Someone curses as a famous linguist turns to face the US president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses NOAM to MAON, and 'round' puts it around DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth president of the United States, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Terrible draw Fulham conceded

indicators.note: conceded suggests the words give up a run of letters held within them

explanation.surface: A football fan laments that Fulham let in an equaliser and only drew.
explanation.walkthrough: Fulham is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful is a straight synonym for terrible or very bad.

clue.text: Serpent I encountered in pub, dazed and confused

indicators.note: in places the snake and I inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Meeting a snake in a pub leaves the drinker bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a spin is an idiom for being flustered and unable to think straight.

clue.text: I look into Repton after ex pupil's historical attempt to cheat

indicators.note: after means the school with I follows the old boy

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: look into means I goes into the school's name

explanation.surface: A former pupil investigates the school, uncovering a long-ago bit of cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: Repton is an English public school; OB (old boy) is a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Obreption is an old legal term for obtaining something by fraud or false statement.

clue.text: Hammond's brief flings away from home?

definitions.meaning: Philip Hammond was the UK cabinet minister in charge of relations with other nations, his brief
romances conducted abroad, punning on overseas dealings

explanation.walkthrough: Philip Hammond was British Foreign Secretary 2014-16, so his brief was the nation's dealings overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a government department's remit and, read literally, romantic dalliances abroad.

clue.text: See 8
Spoiled rotten at first, now struggling to get by

indicators.note: at first puts the word for rotten in front

parts.note: rotten can mean ill, unwell
food that has spoiled has gone off

explanation.surface: A child who was indulged when young now finds money tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiled rotten' reads as one phrase about a pampered child; it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of money means having trouble making ends meet; the phrase is an idiom for that.

clue.text: Review of eastern drama using litotes "a workmanlike effort"

indicators.note: a review looks the material over again, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese theatre
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic reviews a Japanese play, praising it with understatement as a decent job.
explanation.walkthrough: Litotes is understatement ('not bad'), a fitting way to call something workmanlike.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names steady, decent labour without glamour, which is what a workmanlike effort is.

clue.text: American dad, English father

parts.note: pop is an American word for father

explanation.surface: Comparing what an American and an English person call their father.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of the Catholic Church is called the Holy Father, so father is a title for him.

clue.text: Total failure of Sofia Coppola's earliest work

indicators.note: work as a verb means knead or shape, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: earliest means only the opening letter of the director's surname is used

explanation.surface: A jibe that Sofia Coppola's first film was a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earliest work' reads as her debut film, but 'earliest' takes C from Coppola and 'work' rearranges SOFIA plus C.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a complete and humiliating disaster, a total failure.

clue.text: Wearing false tooth is a contractual obligation

parts.note: in can mean wearing, as in 'in a hat'
a denture is a false tooth or set of them

explanation.surface: Wearing a false tooth is an obligation written into someone's contract.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a legal contract, especially binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Caper after gypsy man; it's wild and fantastic

indicators.note: after means the caper comes behind the man

parts.note: Rom is a Romani man
an antic is a playful caper

explanation.surface: A prank follows a traveller, and it is wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic can mean fanciful and unrealistic, like an extravagant wild imagination.

clue.text: A comedian upset an entire nation

indicators.note: upset means the words are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A comic offends a whole country.
explanation.definitionFit: North Macedonia, formerly called Macedonia, is a Balkan country, so it is an example of a nation.

clue.text: Rover susceptible to this dual tyre burst

indicators.note: burst means the tyre blows apart and its letters scatter

explanation.surface: A Land Rover is prone to a blowout of its twin tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' suggests the car; here it means a person with a roving eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is someone who strays from a partner, and so is prone to cheating on a spouse.

clue.text: Latvian head of state's correspondence

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen, the head of state, plus S for the possessive

explanation.surface: The Latvian president's mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence means written communications sent between people, i.e. mail.

clue.text: 50 Cent's about to welcome Knut as a hanger-on

indicators.note: to welcome means the coin takes the other letters inside

parts.note: the coin name cent, with the possessive as link, gives the outer letters
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
the setter Knut refers to himself, giving I

explanation.surface: The rapper 50 Cent is about to greet the setter as a groupie.
explanation.walkthrough: 50 Cent is an American rapper; the number and the coin split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A client can mean a dependant or follower, someone attached to a patron, so a hanger-on.

clue.text: Kill off Frenchman in a stroke of misfortune

indicators.note: in puts the Frenchman inside the rearranged word
off sends the first letter of the word away to the end

parts.note: taken as written
Luc is a French man's name

explanation.surface: Killing a Frenchman with one blow is a terrible turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' moves K from the front of KILL to the back, giving ILLK; LUC goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a direct synonym for bad fortune, an unlucky lot.

clue.text: One given biting criticism and told to buzz off

definitions.text: One given biting criticism and told to buzz off

parts.words: One given biting criticism and told to buzz off
parts.note: describes a small biting insect that people swat away and tell to go

explanation.definitionFit: This small fly bites and buzzes, so it is criticised for biting and told to be gone.

clue.text: A member of the World Chess Federation left it; why? I heard for cheating

parts.words: A member of the World Chess Federation
parts.note: FIDE is the World Chess Federation, and a member is in it

indicators.note: I heard signals the word why is spoken and only its sound kept

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Y

explanation.surface: A chess federation member quit, and someone asks why: allegedly cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: IN FIDE is a member of FIDE; why sounds like the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfaithfulness to a partner is the usual sense; it is cheating on them.

clue.text: Fastnet, say, has tenants

definitions.meaning: the Fastnet Rock is a small rocky isle off southern Ireland, an example
a property that has tenants is rented out

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as IS LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastnet is a tiny island off Ireland; and a property with tenants is let.

clue.text: Riding for a place?

definitions.meaning: a Yorkshire riding was one of three divisions of the county; the word comes from Old Norse for a three-way part
in a race, finishing in the placings, e.g. bronze position

explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was historically split into three Ridings (North, East, West), each one of three parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Riding was one of three parts of Yorkshire; and coming in behind first and second gains a place.

clue.text: "Golden light ale", our American brew

indicators.note: brew means these letters are stirred together into a new mix

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An advert for a pale American beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golden light ale' reads as a beer; the definition is just the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An aureola is a halo of golden radiance around a holy figure's head.

clue.text: Model quits abusin' drug

indicators.note: quits means that letter leaves the word

parts.note: abusing someone verbally is insulting them, with the dropped g as in the clue
the Model T was the classic Ford car, giving T

explanation.surface: A model gives up drug abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe on 'abusin'' tells you to drop the G from the synonym too.
explanation.definitionFit: This hormone is given as a medicine to treat diabetes, so it is a drug.

clue.text: It's found in search; Lord Coe "ashen-faced", according to Spooner

indicators.note: according to Spooner means the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the athlete turned peer, is known as Seb
someone ashen-faced has gone white

explanation.surface: The athletics chief Lord Coe has gone pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Coe is Sebastian Coe, British Olympic runner and sports administrator.
explanation.definitionFit: A web search returns pages from places on the internet, so one turns up in search results.

clue.text: Two journalists (not Brooks and Coulson) got through security

parts.note: a hack is a journalist
Ed is short for editor, another newspaper person

explanation.surface: Two reporters, not the famous phone-hackers, breached a system.
explanation.walkthrough: Rebekah Brooks and Andy Coulson were News of the World editors in the UK phone-hacking scandal, hence the playful exclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To break into a computer system is to get past its protection illicitly.
